data.title: IREN Limited drops 16% amid broad technology selloff
data.description:
AI-cloud provider IREN Limited (IREN) slid almost 16% on Friday. The stock traded at $12.12 in afternoon action, dropping $2.29 on the day and touching a new 52-week low of $12.06.

The decline coincided with a broad technology selloff. The technology sector ETF XLK fell almost 6% and QQQ lost more than 4%. IREN peers CRWV, AMD, NVDA and AVGO each declined roughly 10% to 12%.

data.title: Eastman Chemical cut to Sell equivalent, Celanese maintained Overweight at J.P. Morgan
data.description:
Eastman Chemicals (EMN) fell 3.3% in Friday's trading as J.P. Morgan downgraded shares to Underweight from Neutral with a $62 price target, trimmed from $65, saying the company's larger markets are not growing and its spreads are under pressure.

Global auto production is declining, the domestic housing market is battling high interest rates, and Eastman's (EMN) commodity businesses are experiencing narrowed spreads in propane and propylene, JPM analyst Jeffrey Zekauskas said, adding that he believes it will be difficult for the company to keep up with the market under those conditions.

The company currently delivers a 7% free cash flow yield and offers a substantial 5.44% dividend yield, and the analyst expects Eastman (EMN) to generate a 6%-7% free cash flow yield for 2027.

Zekauskas maintained an Overweight rating on Celanese (CE), which would throw off a 9% free cash flow yield at his $79 PT and trade on a consolidated basis at 7.5x-8.5x EBITDA consistent with the company's historical trading multiples.

data.title: MasTec drops 10% on $1.25B Murphy deal
data.description:
Infrastructure construction firm MasTec (MTZ) shed 10% on Friday following its announcement of a deal to acquire mechanical contractor Murphy. The stock traded at $147.98, a retreat of $16.78 in afternoon action. The decline also coincided with a general pullback in the overall market, led by a selloff in AI-related names.

MasTec said it would acquire Murphy for approximately $1.25 billion in cash, a purchase intended to expand its presence in aviation, defense, pharmaceutical, healthcare, technology and advanced-manufacturing infrastructure. Murphy is expected to become a new operating group within MasTec's Clean Energy and Infrastructure segment, and its management team is expected to remain in place, according to the definitive agreement announcement.

data.title: Will bonds work in a tech crash? Citi weighs in
data.description:
Whether government bonds (SHY) (IEF) (TLT) (ZROZ) will function as an effective portfolio hedge during an equity market (SPY) (QQQ) (DIA) selloff depends heavily on country selection, according to Citi Research, which warns that mounting AI (AIQ) (AIEQ) ecosystem debt and extreme factor rotations threaten stock valuations while high U.S. interest rates limit Treasury protection.

Citi strategist Dirk Willer pointed to a sharp double-digit selloff in copper (CPER) over 10 trading days as a key business-cycle warning. Historically, Willer wrote in a Friday note, similar copper drops precede major bond rallies while equity markets remain subdued. Because copper typically peaks roughly two months after manufacturing PMIs, the signal suggests the July ISM high is already in.

However, because the Federal Reserve remains too hawkish for comfort, Citi cautioned against relying on U.S. Treasuries, preferring duration in Australia (EWA) (adding a five-year AUD receiver at 4.81%) and Canada (EWC) (reiterating a two-year CAD receiver at 3.20%) to capture fixed-income upside during an equity drawdown.

The urgency for bond protection stems from intensifying strain around AI infrastructure. Despite solid operational results, Nvidia (NVDA) failed to reassure markets about its expanding financing commitments. With the semiconductor giant disclosing $32B of neocloud compute backstops and accounting for 27.2% of global venture capital deal value in 2026 year-to-date (up from 7.1% in 2025), concerns are growing over ecosystem debt sustainability and revenue dependence on China (MCHI), which represents about 10% of revenue via customer headquarters.

At the same time, Citi's quantitative framework is flashing rare signals of a potential market peak. Factor price action matches conditions seen at only three previous market tops—February 2000, September 2021, and May 2026—when quality (QUAL) and value (IVE) decoupled from momentum (MTUM) and growth (SPYG) factors. Furthermore, the firm's proprietary "Generals" indicator, designed to detect bubble leadership breakdowns, is on day four of triggering, with four of the top seven S&P 500 (SPY) (VOO) constituents by market cap trading below their 200-day moving averages.

Wall Street’s major averages were markedly lower on Friday, as an extended tech-led selloff is putting the main indices on track for their steepest weekly declines in over a year. The S&P 500, in particular, entered correction territory, declining just over 10% from its October all-time highs. U.S. Treasury yields tumbled across the curve, with the benchmark 10-year tenor back to below 5%, as equities came further under pressure.

Geopolitical risks further complicate multi-asset hedging. Oil (USO) (BNO) markets have priced out Iran escalation risk—Brent is down nearly 20% since its pre-midterms peak—even as hostilities have escalated, including Iranian strikes on Bahrain and U.S. retaliation on Qeshm Island. To manage these overlapping threats, Citi closed its European equity long position and added an oil upside hedge to backstop its overseas rate receiver trades.

data.title: Matthews CEO expects material Axian revenue beginning in fiscal 2028 as company targets operating and cash improvements
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Matthews International (MATW) Q4 fiscal 2026

Management View

  • “This is my first earnings call as President and CEO of Matthews International.” (President, CEO & Director Michael Whitehead) Whitehead credited outgoing CEO Joe Bartolacci and said after site visits he saw “strong businesses with long-standing customer relationships and real competitive advantages,” alongside “room to operate better, improve our financial performance.”
  • Whitehead said fiscal 2026 finished near the company’s August profitability range: “We finished fiscal 2026 with adjusted EBITDA of $161.5 million, near the upper end of the $158 million to $162 million range we established in August.” (President, CEO & Director Whitehead)
  • Whitehead highlighted Memorialization profitability and a stance not reliant on end-market recovery: “We are not counting on a recovery in death rates or traditional burial volumes. We're focused on what we can control: productivity, cost, pricing, innovation, and customer service.” (President, CEO & Director Whitehead)
  • Whitehead reframed Axian timing and milestones: “We continue to believe in Axian's long-term potential, but commercialization is taking longer than expected… We currently expect retailer testing during fiscal 2027, with material Axian revenue beginning in fiscal 2028.” (President, CEO & Director Whitehead)
  • Whitehead described the energy-storage update and cost actions: “We previously said customer testing of our MEODEO mass production line will begin in October. That testing has now begun with multiple customers… we're aligning costs with current demand. Our restructuring in Germany is underway and is expected to be completed during fiscal 2027.” (President, CEO & Director Whitehead)
  • “For the fourth fiscal quarter of 2026, the company reported a net loss of $19.5 million, or $0.62 per share… Consolidated sales for the fourth fiscal quarter of 2026 were $257 million… Consolidated adjusted EBITDA for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 was $46.5 million.” (CFO & Treasurer Daniel Stopar)

Outlook

  • Matthews did not issue formal fiscal 2027 guidance on the call; Whitehead said, “I've been here a little more than 2 months, and I want to take the time to evaluate the businesses and develop a comprehensive plan with our leadership team. On our next earnings call, I look forward to sharing more about our priorities and actions we intend to take.” (President, CEO & Director Whitehead)
  • Whitehead provided timing expectations for key initiatives: “We currently expect retailer testing during fiscal 2027, with material Axian revenue beginning in fiscal 2028.” (President, CEO & Director Whitehead) He also said the company expects “work to progress in fiscal 2027” on Propelis exit strategies, with proceeds intended for debt reduction. (President, CEO & Director Whitehead)
  • In Q&A, Whitehead indicated Memorialization expectations for fiscal 2027 without numerical guidance: “I would think that… that's a pretty flattish market. But I would expect that we would grow on the top line, and I would expect that from a margin profile perspective, we get better.” (President, CEO & Director Whitehead)

Financial Results

  • Stopar attributed year-over-year Q4 changes to portfolio and non-recurring items: “This favorable change was driven by improved operating performance, lower interest and income tax expenses, and charges incurred in the prior year… that did not recur this year.” (CFO & Treasurer Stopar)
  • Segment performance drivers were led by Memorialization execution and Industrial Technologies pressure from divestitures: “Memorialization segment adjusted EBITDA for the current quarter was $47 million… The increase was due to improved operational performance of the cremation equipment business.” (CFO & Treasurer Stopar) “Adjusted EBITDA for the Industrial Technologies segment for the current quarter was a loss of $3.1 million… primarily resulted from the impact of the warehouse automation divestiture.” (CFO & Treasurer Stopar)
  • Cash flow and leverage were framed as key investor focus areas: “Cash flow used in operating activities for the year ended September 30, 2026, was $58 million.” (CFO & Treasurer Stopar) “Outstanding debt… was $610.4 million, and net debt… was $584.3 million.” (CFO & Treasurer Stopar)
  • Capital return policy continued: “the Board declared this week a quarterly dividend of $0.26 per share… This marks the 33rd consecutive annual increase in the company's dividend rate.” (CFO & Treasurer Stopar)

Q&A

  • Dan Moore, CJS Securities: asked about Memorialization margin sustainability and upside; President, CEO & Director Whitehead: “I feel very good about the current margin. I only see upside from there,” citing “complexity in our demand planning” and “distribution network” plus purchasing leverage opportunities.
  • Dan Moore, CJS Securities: asked about TAM expansion via casting; President, CEO & Director Whitehead: pointed to “sports and entertainment memorialization” and “replacement parts… casted replacement parts,” adding, “The barrier to entry is pretty low… due to our 3D printing of molds.”
  • Liam Burke, B. Riley: asked about DBE customer cadence amid the Tesla overhang; President, CEO & Director Whitehead: “the level of interest remains strong,” but “people making large capital investments are not going to do it with a large uncertainty hanging over their heads.”
  • Liam Burke, B. Riley: asked about Axian outlook into 2028; President, CEO & Director Whitehead: “meaningful revenue change from Axian is really more of a 2028 type of timeframe,” while aiming to penetrate CPG with “a full portfolio of products.”
  • Jasper Bibb, Truist: asked what decisions remain and when a full plan arrives; President, CEO & Director Whitehead: highlighted portfolio evaluation, “the Tesla litigation,” and “getting the debt under control,” adding, “it’s a lot of internal focus this coming year.”
  • Jasper Bibb, Truist: asked about Propelis exit timeline; CFO & Treasurer Stopar: “We still expect to be in market in 2027,” while noting synergies are progressing “perhaps at a slightly lower pace than the original business plan.”
  • Justin Bergner, Gabelli Funds: asked about derivative liabilities; CFO & Treasurer Stopar: “Those 2 remaining are off of our books,” while noting “another foreign currency hedge… comes due next year.”
  • Dan Moore, CJS Securities: asked for Industrial revenue breakdown; CFO & Treasurer Stopar: “product ID is about $26 million… engineering is roughly $16 million.”
  • Justin Bergner, Gabelli Funds: asked about stranded costs and ERP; CFO & Treasurer Stopar: cited “about a $2 million year-on-year improvement in our corporate cost structure” and said Matthews is “exploring an alternative [ERP] that would be less complex and… significantly cheaper.”

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts were focused on execution risk and uncertainty, repeatedly pressing on Tesla/DBE timing, Axian commercialization timing, debt reduction, and the Propelis exit; questions emphasized cadence, timelines, and “overhang” language such as “Tesla has been an overhang.” (Liam Burke, B. Riley)
  • Management tone in prepared remarks was confident but acknowledged gaps, with Whitehead stating, “Cash generation fell short of our expectations,” and emphasizing internal control levers; in Q&A, he was more assertive on operational upside: “I only see upside from there.” (President, CEO & Director Whitehead)
  • Versus the prior quarter’s more defensive framing around multiple risks hitting at once (“this was a difficult quarter… all four of those identified risks affected us negatively,” per former CEO Bartolacci), the current call shifted to a new-CEO evaluation phase and fewer explicit near-term commitments, paired with clearer long-dated milestones (fiscal 2027 testing; fiscal 2028 material Axian revenue). (CEO, President & Director Joseph Bartolacci; President, CEO & Director Whitehead)

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Leadership changed: Q3 was led by “CEO, President & Director Joseph Bartolacci,” who said he intended “to retire in the near future,” while Q4 was led by Whitehead as “our company's new President and Chief Executive Officer.” (CEO, President & Director Bartolacci; CFO & Treasurer Stopar)
  • Guidance posture shifted: Q3 included a full-year adjusted EBITDA range of “$158 million to $162 million,” while Q4 emphasized the company finished near that range and is “not providing guidance at this time” in Q&A, pending a broader plan. (CEO, President & Director Bartolacci; President, CEO & Director Whitehead)
  • Key topic continuity remained around Tesla/energy storage and Propelis, but Q4 introduced a more explicit Axian revenue timing statement (“material Axian revenue beginning in fiscal 2028”) and a stated intent to use Propelis proceeds to reduce debt. (President, CEO & Director Whitehead)

Risks and Concerns

  • Whitehead flagged execution and cash conversion: “Cash generation fell short of our expectations,” and said improving conversion and flexibility is “a priority.” (President, CEO & Director Whitehead)
  • The company cited market and cost pressure: “Casket volumes were softer, material and tariff-related costs were higher, and some industrial customers delayed investments.” (President, CEO & Director Whitehead)
  • The energy-storage business faced legal uncertainty: “uncertainty surrounding the ongoing intellectual property dispute has delayed customer investment,” with management focused on demonstrating commercial-scale performance and completing Germany restructuring during fiscal 2027. (President, CEO & Director Whitehead)
  • Propelis timing and outcomes were framed as market-dependent: “Timing and outcome will depend on market conditions and the results of that process.” (President, CEO & Director Whitehead)

Final Takeaway

Management emphasized a leadership transition and an execution reset centered on “focus, simplify, and drive,” with priorities to improve operating performance, increase cash generation, and reduce debt. Whitehead highlighted Memorialization’s profitability and operational upside, a slower-than-expected Axian commercialization path with “material Axian revenue beginning in fiscal 2028,” and a continued push to resolve Tesla-related uncertainty that is delaying energy-storage commitments. CFO Stopar underscored Q4 losses, divestiture-driven sales changes, ongoing leverage levels, and continued dividend increases, while management reiterated an expected Propelis marketing process “in 2027” with proceeds intended for debt paydown.
